title.value: How Should We Extract Discrete Audio Tokens from Self-Supervised Models?
title.justification: The title is directly stated at the beginning of the paper and indicates the focus on extracting discrete audio tokens from self-supervised models.
title.quote: How Should We Extract Discrete Audio Tokens from Self-Supervised Models?

analysis.description: This paper explores the optimal configuration of semantic tokens across discriminative and generative tasks, proposing a scalable vocoder and an attention mechanism to enhance the adaptability and performance of semantic tokens in diverse audio applications.

type.justification: The paper involves practical exploration and evaluation of different techniques for discrete audio token extraction in various tasks, as evidenced by experimental results and comparisons.
type.quote: This paper addresses this gap by evaluating the effects of different heuristics required to derive semantic tokens for several discriminative and generative tasks.

name.justification: The primary focus is on audio and speech processing, exploring discrete audio tokens and their application in speech-related tasks.
name.quote: Learning effective, efficient, and robust representations is a core problem in modern audio and speech processing systems.

name.justification: A significant aspect of the paper is the exploration of representations extracted from self-supervised models.
name.quote: Discrete audio tokens have recently gained attention for their potential to bridge the gap between audio and language processing.

name.justification: ASR is one of the discriminative tasks highlighted in the paper for the application of discrete tokens.
name.quote: Semantic tokens primarily capture coarse information such as phonetic, semantics, and syntactic details.

name.justification: The paper discusses generative tasks like text-to-speech, which is a component of speech synthesis.
name.quote: we focus on text-to-speech and speech enhancement.

name.justification: Wav2Vec2 is mentioned as one of the SSL models from which representations are derived for tokenization.
name.quote: Over the past few years, continuous representations learned by large self-supervised models such as Wav2Vec2 [2], WavLM [3], and HuBERT [4] have achieved unprecedented performance.

is_contributed.justification: Wav2Vec2 is not a contribution of this paper but referenced for its SSL capabilities.
is_contributed.quote: Over the past few years, continuous representations learned by large self-supervised models such as Wav2Vec2 [2]...

is_executed.justification: The paper discusses using representations from models like Wav2Vec2 in experiments, indicating execution.
is_executed.quote: This paper addresses this gap by evaluating the effects of different heuristics required to derive semantic tokens for several discriminative and generative tasks.

is_compared.justification: Wav2Vec2 is compared as part of evaluating different tokenization strategies across tasks.
is_compared.quote: Our results show that the scalable vocoder outperforms all vocoders trained on every specific layer.

name.justification: HiFi-GAN is adapted for use as a scalable vocoder in the paper's experiments.
name.quote: To train such a model, we modify HiFi-GAN [16] to accept a variable number of multi-layer discrete tokens as input.

is_contributed.justification: HiFi-GAN is an existing model that was modified for the study, not newly contributed.
is_contributed.quote: To train such a model, we modify HiFi-GAN [16] to accept a variable number of multi-layer discrete tokens as input.

is_executed.justification: HiFi-GAN's adaptation and use as a vocoder in experiments reflect its execution.
is_executed.quote: This approach is achieved through a layer dropout training scheme, inspired by the bitrate scalability mechanism used in SoundStream.

is_compared.justification: HiFi-GAN's performance is compared to other vocoders in the study.
is_compared.quote: Our results cover findings from two distinct setups: 1) a scalable vocoder trained across five layers, and 2) a vocoder trained on a single layer.
